### M3-E01 · Insert the first artwork

> **SOURCE · demonstrated in the lecture**  
> Source: [lecture3 L130-153](../../sources/lecture3.txt) *“The accession number that we gave it was 56.257.”*

| Topic / concepts | Difficulty | Skills | Dataset | Task type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C3.1 | ★ | INSERT INTO | `mfa` | change the database |

The `collections` table is empty. The museum acquires **Profusion of Flowers**, accession number `56.257`, acquired `1956-04-12`.
Insert it with **id 1**, listing all four columns explicitly.

<details><summary>Setup the checker runs first</summary>

```sql
DELETE FROM "created"; DELETE FROM "collections";
```
</details>

`SELECT * FROM "collections"`

| id | title | accession_number | acquired |

| 1 | Profusion of Flowers | 56.257 | 1956-04-12 |

</details>

### M3-E06 · From an imported CSV into the real table

> **SOURCE · demonstrated in the lecture**  
> Source: [lecture3 L570-603](../../sources/lecture3.txt) *“I actually have a way to dynamically select all the values I want to insert”*, [lecture3 L644-663](../../sources/lecture3.txt) *“it won't be converted to”*

|---|---|---|---|---|

You imported `database/csv/mfa_noid.csv` (no id column) into a new table `temp`, as in the lecture.
1. Copy all of its rows into `collections` so that SQLite generates the ids. Turn the empty-string acquisition date into a real `NULL` while copying.
2. Drop `temp`.

<details><summary>Setup the checker runs first</summary>

```sql
DELETE FROM "created"; DELETE FROM "collections";
-- What `.import --csv mfa_noid.csv temp` produces: every value is TEXT, and blanks are '' (not NULL)
CREATE TABLE "temp" ("title" TEXT, "accession_number" TEXT, "acquired" TEXT);
INSERT INTO "temp" VALUES
  ('Profusion of Flowers', '56.257', '1956-04-12'),
  ('Farmers Working at Dawn', '11.6152', '1911-08-03'),
  ('Spring Outing', '14.76', '1914-01-08'),
  ('Imaginative Landscape', '56.496', ''),
  ('Peonies and Butterfly', '06.1899', '1906-01-01');
```
</details>

<details><summary>Expected output (try first!)</summary>

After your SQL, the checker runs:

`SELECT "title", "accession_number", "acquired" FROM "collections"`

| title | accession_number | acquired |
|---|---|---|
| Profusion of Flowers | 56.257 | 1956-04-12 |
| Farmers Working at Dawn | 11.6152 | 1911-08-03 |
| Spring Outing | 14.76 | 1914-01-08 |
| Imaginative Landscape | 56.496 | NULL |
| Peonies and Butterfly | 06.1899 | 1906-01-01 |

`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE "name" = 'temp'`

|---|
| 0 |

`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "collections" WHERE "acquired" IS NULL`

|---|
| 1 |

</details>

### M3-E09 · Delete an artist the two-step way

> **SOURCE · demonstrated in the lecture**  
> Source: [lecture3 L954-979](../../sources/lecture3.txt) *“First delete their affiliation, then delete their name.”*

| Topic / concepts | Difficulty | Skills | Dataset | Task type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C3.5, C3.6, C1.4 | ★★★ | DELETE, subquery, FOREIGN KEY | `mfa` | change the database |

Remove **Unidentified artist** completely. `created` has no ON DELETE action here, so deleting the artist first fails.
Do it in the right order, and **don't hard-code the artist's id**.

<details><summary>Setup the checker runs first</summary>

```sql
-- rebuild "created" WITHOUT ON DELETE CASCADE (the first version in the lecture)
DROP TABLE "created";
CREATE TABLE "created" (
    "artist_id" INTEGER, "collection_id" INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY("artist_id") REFERENCES "artists"("id"),
    FOREIGN KEY("collection_id") REFERENCES "collections"("id")
);
INSERT INTO "created" VALUES (1, 2), (3, 1), (2, 3), (2, 4);
```
</details>

<details><summary>Expected output (try first!)</summary>

After your SQL, the checker runs:

`SELECT * FROM "artists"`

| id | name |
|---|---|
| 1 | Li Yin |
| 2 | Placeholder Artist |

`SELECT * FROM "created"`

| artist_id | collection_id |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2 |
| 2 | 3 |
| 2 | 4 |

</details>

### M3-E13 · Clean the votes and get four groups

> **SOURCE · demonstrated in the lecture**  
> Source: [lecture3 L1281-1299](../../sources/lecture3.txt) *“takes a string and just removes leading and trailing”*, [lecture3 L1384-1394](../../sources/lecture3.txt) *“so be careful with this”*, [lecture3 L1444-1448](../../sources/lecture3.txt) *“Farmers Working At Dawn has six votes.”*

| Topic / concepts | Difficulty | Skills | Dataset | Task type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C3.8 | ★★★ | UPDATE, trim, upper, LIKE | `votes` | change the database |

The `votes` table holds 20 typed-in votes with stray spaces, inconsistent capitals and typos.
Write UPDATE statements so that `SELECT "title", COUNT(*) FROM "votes" GROUP BY "title";` returns exactly four groups:
*Farmers Working at Dawn*, *Imaginative Landscape*, *Profusion of Flowers*, *Spring Outing*.
Capitalization is up to you; the checker compares case-insensitively but requires no leading or trailing spaces.

<details><summary>Expected output (try first!)</summary>

After your SQL, the checker runs:

`SELECT upper("title"), COUNT(*) FROM "votes" GROUP BY upper("title")`

| upper("title") | COUNT(*) |
|---|---|
| FARMERS WORKING AT DAWN | 6 |
| IMAGINATIVE LANDSCAPE | 5 |
| PROFUSION OF FLOWERS | 5 |
| SPRING OUTING | 4 |

`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "votes" WHERE "title" != trim("title")`

| COUNT(*) |
|---|
| 0 |

</details>

### M3-E14 · Triggers that log sales and purchases

> **SOURCE · demonstrated in the lecture**  
> Source: [lecture3 L1588-1631](../../sources/lecture3.txt) *“So automatically, I added "Profusion of Flowers"”*, [lecture3 L1638-1678](../../sources/lecture3.txt) *“So this is the power of triggers.”*

| Topic / concepts | Difficulty | Skills | Dataset | Task type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C3.9 | ★★★ | CREATE TRIGGER, OLD, NEW | `mfa` | change the database |

1. Create `transactions(id INTEGER primary key, title TEXT, action TEXT)`.
2. Create trigger **sell**: *before* a row is deleted from `collections`, insert its title with action `'sold'`.
3. Create trigger **buy**: *after* a row is inserted into `collections`, insert its title with action `'bought'`.

The checker then deletes *Profusion of Flowers* and re-inserts it, and inspects `transactions`.

<details><summary>Expected output (try first!)</summary>

After your SQL, the checker runs:

`SELECT "title", "action" FROM "transactions" ORDER BY "id"`

| title | action |
|---|---|

_(no rows)_

</details>
